title: Cohort Watchtower: probabilistic rollback autopilot for canary & A/B
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a probabilistic, cohort-aware automatic rollback system (Cohort Watchtower) that evaluates quality regressions during canary and A/B rollouts and executes staged rollback policies. The goal is to reduce time-to-revert for true regressions while avoiding noisy false positives from natural traffic drift.
background: Current rollout gates rely on simple threshold checks that are brittle to traffic shifts, small sample sizes, and metric seasonality. We frequently either overreact to transient noise or under-react to slow but meaningful regressions. This ticket defines an orchestration + statistics layer that combines Bayesian effect-size estimation, cohort stratification, and multi-stage remediation (soft degrade -> hard rollback).
proposed_solution: Build a Cohort Watchtower service which: 1) assigns live traffic into stratified cohorts (geo, device, route, customer tier) and maintains per-cohort metric baselines; 2) runs an adaptive Bayesian test for each metric comparing candidate vs baseline with a configurable minimum detectable effect; 3) uses probabilistic rules (posterior probability of regression > X%) to trigger mitigation; 4) performs staged remediation: a) reduce candidate traffic weight by a factor, b) reroute to fallback variant for affected cohorts, c) full rollback if signal persists past a recovery window; 5) provides human-in-loop hooks in Console and Slack with recommended actions and rollback rationale.
technical_design_notes: - Statistical engine: hierarchical Bayesian model that pools information across cohorts while allowing per-cohort offsets. Default priors calibrated from historical evals. - Metrics: support scalar metrics (accuracy, BLEU-like scores), latency p95, token error rate, and business signals (API error rate, cost-per-call). - Significance criteria: posterior probability (candidate worse than baseline by > delta) > 0.975 triggers soft action; > 0.999 after cooldown triggers hard rollback. - Minimum sample window: configurable (default 15 minutes) and minimum examples per cohort (default 200 requests). - Implementation: new microservice written in Go for ingest/decision, Rust for sampling library optional; store time-series in existing TSDB and model state in Redis for fast lookups. - Integrations: rollout controller (existing rollout API), Console for visual diff, Alerting system for on-call, and audit logs to Private's audit pipeline (KMS-encrypted).
rollout_plan: Phase 1: shadow mode (2 weeks) — decisions logged but no automated traffic change, surface false-positives for calibration. Phase 2: soft-degrade enabled for non-critical routes (4 weeks) — automated weight reductions only. Phase 3: full autopilot on low-risk customers, with manual approval for enterprise tenants. Phase 4: extend to Dedicated pools and Private deployments after security review.
acceptance_criteria: Service runs in shadow mode for 14 days and produces decision logs for at least 100 rollouts
Posterior estimation latency < 200ms for a typical cohort query (95th percentile)
Soft-degrade actions succeed in 99% of trials during canary experiments in sandbox environment
A/B experiments with injected regressions are automatically reduced in traffic weight within configured SLAs (median time-to-first-mitigate < 5 minutes)
Audit trail is written for every decision and visible in Console rollout timeline
monitoring_alerts: Shadow mode false-positive ratio exceeds 5% over 24h
tasks: Design and validate hierarchical Bayesian model (statistics)
Implement decision API and experiment ingestion endpoint
Wire metrics from TSDB and define schema for per-cohort baselines
Implement staged mitigation actions in rollout controller
Console UI: decision rationale + one-click override
E2E tests with synthetic regressions and traffic replay
Run security review for Private deployments
timeline: Week 1-2: modeling + API prototype. Week 3: integration with rollout controller + shadow runs. Week 4-6: soft-degrade experiments and tuning. Week 7-8: enterprise canary pilots and audit review.
risks: Model miscalibration causing noisy mitigations — mitigated by extended shadow mode and manual overrides
Insufficient cohort sample sizes leading to delayed detection — mitigated by adaptive pooling and minimum sample thresholds
Automation triggering during upstream infra incidents (not model regressions) — mitigated by cross-checks against infra health signals
Console UX causing operator confusion — mitigated by clear rationale and confidence scores on UI
